bug_description.original: A heap-use-after-free exists in libxml2's error reporting: xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal (error.c) can read from parser input pointers that reference freed heap memory when invoked via xmlReportError/__xmlRaiseError. This results in reads of deallocated memory during parsing (e.g., while handling entities or external subsets), leading to crashes or other undefined behavior and potentially enabling exploitation.
bug_description.normalized: When parsing XML that loads an external entity, a failed grow of the entity input buffer can free or replace the old buffer storage while leaving `xmlParserInput` pointers stale. Error reporting later prints file context from those stale pointers, and `xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal` dereferences freed heap memory.

source.value_from: attacker-controlled external entity bytes provided through the XML testcase
source.description: The external entity loader materializes attacker-controlled entity bytes by storing the supplied memory buffer pointer into the parser input buffer context without copying it.

root_cause.description: When buffer growth has failed and `buf->error` is set, `xmlBufResetInput` returns without clearing the parser input pointers, leaving `input->base`, `input->cur`, and `input->end` aliased to the old freed allocation.

sink.description: The error-reporting file-context printer walks bytes through `cur`, which was derived from stale parser input pointers and now points into freed heap memory.

tainted_value_origin.description: The external entity bytes from the testcase enter project code as the in-memory parser input buffer source.

fine_trace.note: The parser input buffer for an in-memory document or entity keeps the attacker-controlled byte buffer pointer `mem` in `ctxt->mem`; this is the first project-code materialization of the PoC bytes used by the vulnerable path.

The fuzz entity loader creates an `xmlParserInputBuffer` over `entity->data` for the external entity referenced from the document, so the parser will read attacker-supplied entity bytes through `input->buf`.

After loading the external entity, the parser resets the input stream to the current buffer storage, so `input->base`, `input->cur`, and `input->end` now alias the entity buffer that will later be grown and potentially reallocated.

While `xmlLoadEntityContent` drains the entity input, growing the buffer fails; `xmlBufGrow` has already reallocated away the old storage, and this error path records the failure in `in->error = XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY`.

`xmlLoadEntityContent` immediately calls `xmlBufResetInput(input->buf->buffer, input)` again after the failed grow. In the vulnerable code, the `buf->error` branch returns without updating the input pointers, so they remain stale aliases to the pre-realloc buffer that ASan reports as freed by `xmlBufGrowInternal`.
Because `res < 0`, the parser raises a fatal error while the current parser input still contains the dangling `base/cur/end` pointers for the external entity stream.
Error reporting uses the current parser input from the context and passes it to the file-context printer without checking whether its pointers were invalidated by the failed buffer growth.

The printer derives `cur = input->cur` and then dereferences `*cur` while scanning the line for display. Since `input->cur` still points into the freed entity buffer, this loop performs the heap-use-after-free read reported by ASan.

parser_admitted.description: The document is accepted far enough for the parser to enter the DTD/internal-subset state and parse markup declarations, which is required before the external entity declaration and expansion path can run.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: patch and ASan free stack both support that stale parser input pointers survive the failed buffer grow/reset sequence rather than being refreshed

poc.trigger: Run the `xml` reader target on the provided testcase so parsing enters the DTD/internal subset, loads an external entity from the testcase-controlled entity store, hits the failed-grow error path in `xmlLoadEntityContent`, and then reports the error.

format.name: xml
format.contract: The testcase must drive the reader parser through a DOCTYPE/internal-subset path that declares and loads an external entity, then cause `xmlLoadEntityContent` to hit the `res < 0` error path after buffer growth on that entity input so error reporting prints file context from the same input stream.
